chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When the owned slave is blinded, his master should emancipate him, and it would not be for him that he keeps him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave who becomes blind?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the fiqh of 'iklāl' (emancipation due to disability), establishing that blindness renders a slave ineligible for continued servitude, thereby obligating the master to free them. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often discussed alongside other disabilities like leprosy to determine whether emancipation is immediate or discretionary, reflecting the principle of restoring dignity to those unable to fulfill their duties. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith, connecting Imam al-Sadiq to earlier authorities through a robust isnad.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, form Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban, from Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the owned slave is blinded, his master should emancipate him, and it would not be for him that he keeps him’.
